attacks.claim: Unit error: 38M lines/day x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens per day, which is about $1,140 per day at $0.50/1M, not per month. Over 30 days input is about $34,200/month, roughly 23x the $1,500 approved budget, so the 'within budget' conclusion is false.
attacks.evidence: Input: 38M lines x 60 tokens = 2.28B tokens -> ~$1,140 ... Estimated total: ~$1,150/month, within the $1,500 budget.

attacks.claim: No spend ceiling, daily token cap, or volume-triggered sampling is specified. Peak day (61M lines) alone is about $1,830 of input, and summary volume rises during incident storms.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: any daily or monthly spend cap, per-window token cap, or sampling rule. 'peak day 61M'

attacks.claim: Per-call input is unchecked. About 4,400 lines per service per 5-minute window is roughly 264k input tokens (about 420k at peak), which likely exceeds a single call's context. No truncation or chunking strategy is stated.
attacks.evidence: every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt ... ABSENT: context limit, truncation, or chunking.

attacks.claim: log-tap forwards every line to the queue with no bounds, drop policy, or backpressure design. If the summarizer lags during incidents, queue growth is unbounded.
attacks.evidence: forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue ... ABSENT: queue bounds, drop policy, or concurrency limits.

attacks.claim: The auto-comment has no generated-at timestamp or window marker, so a stale or failed summary reads as current. Timeouts, retries, and summarizer-lag alerting are also unspecified.
attacks.evidence: the PagerDuty incident gets an auto-comment with the latest summaries for the paging service and its direct dependencies ... ABSENT: timestamp, timeouts, retries, lag alerting.

attacks.claim: log-tap sits on the production Vector logging path, but the plan does not require it to be non-blocking or bounded. Summarizer backpressure could delay or drop production logs during the incidents when logs matter most.
attacks.evidence: subscribes to the existing Vector pipeline after the redaction stage and forwards every application log line to the summarizer queue ... ABSENT: non-blocking or bounded-buffer requirement.

attacks.claim: Staffing assumes both engineers spend 100% on the build for 6 weeks, but the charter says on-call and interrupt work averages 50% of their time. Effective capacity is about 6 eng-weeks against 12 planned, and there is no backfill or contingency.
attacks.evidence: Staffing: both platform engineers full-time for 6 weeks (2 x 6 = 12 eng-weeks). ... context: on-call/interrupt work averages 50% of their time

attacks.claim: Redaction covers only emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs. The Q1 audit was for the log retention policy, not for egress to a third-party LLM. Names, account IDs, and free-text customer data are not covered, and no pre-transmission verification is specified, yet every line is sent out.
attacks.evidence: already masks emails, tokens, card numbers and IPs for our log retention policy (audited in Q1)

attacks.claim: The DPA reference alone does not show that customer-derived log content may be sent to this vendor. Scope over log data categories, subprocessors, data residency, and customer contract terms is unconfirmed.
attacks.evidence: Corvid account has zero-retention enabled; data processing addendum signed by Legal (ref DPA-0417).

attacks.claim: The goal promises a summary 'within seconds of a page', but the design produces summaries every 5 minutes, so the attached summary can be up to 5 minutes plus LLM latency old. The goal and design contradict each other.
attacks.evidence: within seconds of a page ... every 5 minutes, sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service

attacks.claim: The new production system (log-tap, queue, summarizer, storage, LLM dependency, PagerDuty and service-catalog integrations) has no named post-launch owner, on-call rotation, or SLO. A 2-person team already at 50% interrupt load would absorb it.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: owner, on-call rotation, and SLO for log-tap, the summarizer, and stored summaries after the 6-week build.

attacks.claim: No written rollback or kill-switch procedure covers log-tap, the summarizer, and the PagerDuty comment hook separately. Disabling only the summarizer would still ship logs to the vendor, and purge steps for forwarded data and stored summaries are missing.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: rollback, feature flag, kill-switch, and data deletion procedure.

attacks.claim: Summarization depends on one vendor with no fallback or exit path. Because the feature is advisory and fails open to the existing workflow, the impact is loss of the feature rather than an incident-response dependency.
attacks.evidence: Model: Corvid-mini, $0.50 per 1M input tokens, $2.00 per 1M output tokens. ... Summaries are advisory only.

attacks.claim: Log lines are attacker-influenced text placed into the LLM prompt, and the output is posted to PagerDuty without validation or escaping stated. Impact is misleading advisory text, not code execution, so this is minor.
attacks.evidence: sends the last 5 minutes of logs per service to the LLM with a fixed prompt and stores a structured summary

attacks.claim: The launch gate uses 40 retrospective incidents graded by the incident commander, who knows the root cause (hindsight bias). At n=40, 5% misleading is about 2 cases, the interval is wide, and no shadow-mode test is planned. The IC grading time is not staffed.
attacks.evidence: replay the last 40 incidents ... have the incident commander grade it ... Launch gate: >= 70% useful, <= 5% misleading.

attacks.claim: The 15-20 minute grep-time claim and the 47-to-30 minute MTTR target have no measurement method, baseline breakdown, or control, so any MTTR change cannot be attributed to the tool. This is an outcome goal, not a build blocker.
attacks.evidence: instead of spending the first 15-20 minutes grepping logs across 30 services ... median MTTR 47 min -> 30 min within one quarter of launch.

attacks.claim: Stored summaries can carry log fragments, but no retention period, access control, or deletion path is stated.
attacks.evidence: stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy)

attacks.claim: Direct-dependency lookup from the service catalog is hidden coupling. Stale catalog data silently changes which summaries are attached, and catalog accuracy is not verified.
The 'suspected deploy' field needs a deploy-correlation feed that is not listed as a dependency, and its build effort is not estimated.
attacks.evidence: stores a structured summary (top errors, new error signatures, affected endpoints, suspected deploy)
